newsitem.title: CROATIA: Soros pays tax in Croatia after evasion charges.
newsitem.headline: Soros pays tax in Croatia after evasion charges.

text.p: An international humanitarian foundation sponsored by U.S. tycoon George Soros has paid $500,000 in taxes, a month after Croatian financial police charged it with tax evasion, officials said on Saturday.

"We paid the tax demanded by the financial police but under protest and we told them we considered their demand legally unfounded," executive director of the Soros-sponsored Open Society Foundation Srdjan Dvornik told Reuters.
"We did it as a precaution so not to risk further problems our organisation may have in Croatia," he said.
The Foundation paid some 2.5 million kuna of alleged unpaid taxes, including some 300,000 kuna interest for delay in payment, or some $500,000 in total, Dvornik said.

Croatian financial police in December stormed the premises of the organistion in Zagreb and said it found evidence of "illegal financial transactions" that the society had been allegedly performing for the last year.

The police then charged the society with financial malpractice and tax evasion of some $500,000. The Zagreb public prosecutor in January indicted Dvornik and two other senior society officials for falsifying financial records.

The action against the Foundation, which promotes democracy and a free press in the former communist countries of eastern Europe, came after weeks of anti-Soros campaigning initiated by president Franjo Tudjman. In November he branded the Hungarian-born businessman and philanthropist an enemy of the state.
Shortly after that police confiscated $65,000 from Dvornik and another indicted official at a border crossing. The two were released after interrogation but the money was not returned.
The Croatian television said on Friday that by paying the tax the society admitted it had violated the law.
"We did not admit anything. When we get the final decision from the financial police, we'll appeal against it so to get the money back," Dvornik said.
The television said it was unclear whether Soros would also have to pay additional fines for "financial malpractice".
